subject: mathematics
question_text: Draw the graph of y = sin 2x on [−π/2, π/2].

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.87, chapter 8 TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS, Very Short Answer question 28(iii). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The split gives one mark to the period 2π/2 = π with the table of values and one to the drawing itself, since the question asks for a graph. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A prints ten very short answers of 2 marks each and the student writes all ten; Trigonometric Ratios and Transformations supplies two of those slots on almost every paper. recall_prompt: Say how you would draw this one — name the period, the values you plot, and the shape you get.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Period and table of values
steps.margin_note: First mark. The period is π and the given interval has length π, so the picture is exactly one complete period — one dip and one hump.
steps.memory_tip: Period of sin kx is 2π/|k|, so sin 2x repeats every π — and the interval given is exactly π long.
lines: The interval [−π/2, π/2] has length π,
so it holds exactly one full period.

recall.must_convey: That the period of sin 2x is 2π/2 = π, so [−π/2, π/2] holds one full period, with values 0, −1, 0, 1, 0 at −π/2, −π/4, 0, π/4, π/2.

at minus pi by four the value is minus one and at pi by four it is plus one
the values are zero, minus one, zero, one, zero
period pi kabatti interval lo okkate full period vasthundi
state the period and make the table of five values

steps.why: The 2 inside the sine halves the period, so twice as much of the graph fits into the same width. Getting the period first is what fixes how many humps to draw.
common_mistakes: Using 2π as the period, which would draw only half the shape.
Reading sin 2x as 2 sin x, which changes the height instead of the period.

steps.label: Draw the graph
steps.margin_note: Second mark, and the point of the question. One full period: a dip to −1 at x = −π/4, up through the origin, a hump to +1 at x = π/4, and back to 0 at x = π/2.
steps.memory_tip: Zeros at −π/2, 0 and π/2; lowest point at −π/4 and highest at π/4. Dip first, then hump.

recall.must_convey: That the axes are drawn and one full period of y = sin 2x is sketched: zeros at −π/2, 0 and π/2, a minimum of −1 at −π/4 and a maximum of +1 at π/4. Naming the drawing is full credit.
accept: draw the axes then one full period with a dip at minus pi by four and a hump at pi by four
the curve cuts the x axis at minus pi by two, zero and pi by two
sketch the negative hump first and then the positive hump
modata kinda hump, taruvata paina hump, zeros moodu chotla
draw one complete period of sin two x

steps.why: The order matters: on this interval the NEGATIVE half comes first, because sin 2x is negative for every x between −π/2 and 0. Drawing the positive hump first gives the graph of −sin 2x by mistake.
common_mistakes: Drawing the positive hump on the left, which is the graph of −sin 2x.
Drawing only half a period, which is the graph of sin x on this interval.
Taking the height as 2 instead of 1.
